findings.title: Published LLM fine-tuning tutorial reports epsilon 1.09 for an adaptively-clipped run whose true cost is 8.99 — the adaptive-clipping quantile release is never accounted
findings.line: cell 11 (nb JSON lines 420-429, `expected_eps = ...`) and cell 13 (`dp_step = ...`); published output at nb JSON line 377
findings.claim: The flagship 'Fine-tuning an LLM' tutorial trains with `adaptive_clipped_grad(..., target_quantile=0.80, ...)` (default `fraction_noise_std=0.05`, i.e. a noisy clip-rate query released every step) but prices the run with `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(NOISE_MULTIPLIER), sample_rate, truncated_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dataset_size=len(train_dataset)) * NUM_STEPS` — the plain Gaussian chain, with no `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(...)` wrapper. The string `adaclip` does not appear anywhere in the notebook (`grep -c adaclip docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb` -> 0). Opaque's own user guide mandates the opposite: docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249, 'Adaptive clipping introduces an additional privacy cost (the noisy clipping rate query). Account for it using `dpsgd_acc.adaclip()`', and examples/train_dpsgd.py:1553 does exactly that. The notebook therefore publishes a privacy number that omits NUM_STEPS noisy-quantile releases.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader follows the tutorial (the only published LLM example, linked from docs/tutorials/README.md:18 and mkdocs.yml:140), adopts its accounting line for their own adaptive-clipping run, and reports an epsilon roughly 8x below the guarantee their mechanism actually provides. Measured at the notebook's own constants (nm=1.5, q=8/500, truncated_batch_size=12, dataset_size=500, 20 steps, delta=1e-5): the notebook's chain gives epsilon=1.0944 (matching its published 'Expected final epsilon: 1.09'); the same chain with `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.5), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=8)` as inner gives epsilon=8.9928 — an 8.2x understatement. The notebook is not in the CI execution list, and executing it would not catch this anyway: the wrong formula runs without error.
evidence: docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb cell 11: `grad_fn, clip_state = adaptive_clipped_grad(per_example_loss, argnums=0, batch_argnums=(2,3,4), initial_clipping_norm=CLIP_NORM, target_quantile=0.80, ... key=key(0), normalize_by=BATCH_SIZE)` — `fraction_noise_std` left at its 0.05 default (signature: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py, `fraction_noise_std: float = 0.05`)

Same cell: `expected_eps = (dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(NOISE_MULTIPLIER), sample_rate, truncated_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dataset_size=len(train_dataset)) * NUM_STEPS).epsilon_at(TARGET_DELTA)` ; stored output `Expected final epsilon: 1.09`

docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249 prescribes `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.adaclip(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=expected_batch_size), sample_rate)`
examples/train_dpsgd.py:1553 `mechanism = lambda nm, ebs=args.batch_size, ng=_num_groups: dpsgd_acc.adaclip(...)` — the example script does account for it; only the tutorial does not
Measured with the repo venv: notebook chain -> 1.0944 ; adaclip-wrapped chain -> 8.9928 (delta=1e-5)
.github/workflows/pr.yml:290-302 executes only accounting_and_calibration.ipynb, dp_sgd_training.ipynb and dp_ftrl_training.ipynb; llm_finetuning.ipynb is not executed
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the inner mechanism in `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(NOISE_MULTIPLIER), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=BATCH_SIZE)` in both cell 11 and cell 13, re-execute the notebook in place so the published outputs carry the honest number, and add llm_finetuning.ipynb to the pr.yml execution list. Longer term, add an assertion inside the notebook (as examples/quickstart.py:99 does) that ties the reported epsilon to the mechanism actually constructed.

findings.title: API reference defines `dpftrl_acc.poisson`'s `sample_rate` as the whole-dataset per-round probability; the implementation requires the per-active-band conditional rate (up to 100x optimistic epsilon)
findings.line: 468 (`- \`sample_rate\` (float): Poisson sampling probability per round.`); same omission in docs/user-guide/accounting.md:327-340 and 495-512, docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md:73-80 and 103-112, docs/index.md:84-89
findings.claim: `dpftrl_acc.poisson(inner, sample_rate, *, n_steps)` treats `sample_rate` as the inclusion probability *conditional on the active band*, not as the whole-dataset rate. The implementation says so only in a module docstring (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:50-54, 'BandMF requires cyclic sampling over fixed dataset partitions; `sample_rate` is conditional on the active partition'), and the trainer converts explicitly (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:154, `group_rate = float(sample_rate) * local_size / group_size`, i.e. roughly q_global * bands). The API reference bullet says the opposite in plain global terms, and neither docs/user-guide/accounting.md nor docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md nor docs/index.md mentions the conversion anywhere. The only correct statement in the docs tree is a Tips bullet at the bottom of a different page, docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:321-325.
findings.failure_scenario: A user computes `sample_rate = expected_batch_size / dataset_size` — the convention used by every DP-SGD example on the very same pages, and the exact quantity DPTrainer takes — sizes `CyclicPoissonSampler(sample_rate=q_cond, bands=B)` so the realized batch matches, and passes the global q to `dpftrl_acc.poisson`. Nothing raises (q_global < q_cond is always in range), and the reported epsilon is far below the truth. Measured on the configuration published at docs/user-guide/accounting.md:506-510 (band_mf_strategy(bands=64), n_steps=15_624, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5): sample_rate=0.01 gives epsilon=0.9857, while the conditional rate that actually realizes a 1%-of-dataset batch (0.64) gives epsilon=102.1295 — a 104x understatement. At the bands=10 / n_steps=1000 configuration on docs/index.md and docs/reference/accounting.md, 0.7181 vs 7.0469 (9.8x).
evidence: docs/reference/accounting.md:468: `- \`sample_rate\` (float): Poisson sampling probability per round.`

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:50-54 class docstring: 'BandMF requires cyclic sampling over fixed dataset partitions; ``sample_rate`` is conditional on the active partition.'

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:130-163 `_cyclic_poisson_group_rate` — 'Per-active-group conditional rate'; `group_rate = float(sample_rate) * local_size / group_size`
Measured: `dpftrl_acc.poisson(dpftrl_acc.mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=64)), sample_rate=0.01, n_steps=15624).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 0.9857 ; with sample_rate=0.64 = 102.1295
Measured: bands=10, n_steps=1000, nm=1.0 -> q=0.01 gives 0.7181, q=0.1 gives 7.0469
The correct semantics appear only at docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:321-325 ('both take the per-active-group conditional rate (`q` above), not a whole-dataset rate')
findings.fix_sketch: Change the reference bullet to 'per-active-band conditional inclusion probability; for BandMF with `bands` groups this is `expected_batch_size / floor(dataset_size / bands)`, i.e. roughly `bands x` the whole-dataset rate', repeat it in docs/user-guide/accounting.md's `dpftrl_acc.poisson` section and in docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md, and make the worked examples derive the rate from batch size and bands the way docs/tutorials/dp_ftrl_training.ipynb cell 5 already does (`sample_rate = batch_size * bands / n_samples`).

findings.title: Sampling reference states CyclicPoissonSampler has no batch-size cap and that `dpftrl_acc.poisson` matches uncapped draws only — both are false, and the cap silently applies for bands>1 where no accountant supports it
findings.claim: The page asserts 'There is no batch-size cap on this sampler; `dpftrl_acc.poisson` matches uncapped Poisson draws only.' Both halves are false at HEAD. `CyclicPoissonSampler.__init__` accepts `truncated_batch_size: int | None = None` and applies it, and `dpftrl_acc.poisson` accepts `truncated_batch_size` and `dataset_size`. The parameter table at docs/reference/sampling.md:184-190 and docs/user-guide/sampling.md:164-172 both omit the parameter, while the mkdocstrings block on the very same reference page (`::: opaque.dpftrl.sampling.CyclicPoissonSampler`, docs/reference/sampling.md:258) renders the class docstring, which documents the cap ('truncated_batch_size: Optional cap on per-step batch size ... Only the ``bands == 1`` / ``IdentityMf`` combination is supported in :func:`opaque.dpftrl.accounting.poisson`'). The rendered page therefore contradicts itself.
findings.failure_scenario: Library users (the trainer path is fail-closed) can construct `CyclicPoissonSampler(ds, sample_rate=0.5, bands=4, n_steps=20, truncated_batch_size=60, key=...)`; verified, every batch comes back at exactly 60 where the uncapped sampler yields 112-136. `dpftrl_acc.poisson` rejects truncated arguments for BandMfStrategy (ConfigurationError, 'truncated Poisson is only supported for IdentityStrategy inner'), so the user's only option is to account with the plain-Poisson PLD — which is optimistic for a capped sampler. In the DP-SGD analogue on the same docs (docs/user-guide/sampling.md:487) truncation is priced at roughly 2.4x plain Poisson (measured 9.2359 vs 3.8333 at nm=1.1, q=0.032, 500 steps), so the understatement is large. A reader who trusts the reference sentence also never learns that `dpftrl_acc.poisson(..., truncated_batch_size=, dataset_size=)` exists for identity MF.
evidence: docs/reference/sampling.md:194-196: 'account with `dpftrl_acc.poisson(mechanism, sample_rate, n_steps=...)`. There is no batch-size cap on this sampler; `dpftrl_acc.poisson` matches uncapped Poisson draws only.'
`inspect.signature(CyclicPoissonSampler.__init__)` -> `(self, data_source, sample_rate, bands=1, n_steps=1, partition_type=PartitionType.EQUAL_SPLIT, truncated_batch_size: int | None = None, *, key)`
`inspect.signature(opaque.dpftrl.accounting.poisson)` -> `(inner, sample_rate, *, n_steps, truncated_batch_size: int | None = None, dataset_size: int | None = None)`

Executed: `CyclicPoissonSampler(ds, sample_rate=0.5, bands=4, n_steps=20, truncated_batch_size=60, key=key(0))` -> all 20 batch sizes == 60; same sampler without the cap -> [112, 120, 121, 133, 136, ...]

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_poisson.py:15-18 and 68-73 document the cap; packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:120-130 rejects it for BandMfStrategy
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:229-236 rejects the combination in the trainer, so the exposure is the direct library surface only
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the two sentences with the true statement: the sampler accepts `truncated_batch_size`, and it may only be used with `bands == 1` / IdentityStrategy, where `dpftrl_acc.poisson(..., truncated_batch_size=, dataset_size=)` supplies the matching truncated-Poisson PLD; add the parameter to both tables. Separately, make `CyclicPoissonSampler.__init__` raise when `truncated_batch_size is not None and bands > 1`, so the unaccountable configuration cannot be constructed at all.

findings.title: Privacy-auditing tutorial prices a shuffled fixed-batch DataLoader with Poisson amplification and under-counts its own steps — the exact OPQ-355 defect, surviving in the sibling notebook the sweep did not touch
findings.line: cell 9 (nb JSON line 271, `train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)`) and cell 13 (nb JSON lines 372-373)
findings.claim: OPQ-355 ('the Quick Start and the DP-SGD tutorial publish a Poisson-amplified epsilon for a `torch.randperm` shuffled fixed-batch loop, and both under-count steps') was closed as part of sweep #843. It is fixed in docs/getting-started/quickstart.md (now an include of the runnable examples/quickstart.py, which uses PoissonSampler) and in docs/tutorials/dp_sgd_training.ipynb (cell 13 now iterates a PoissonSampler and composes step-exactly). The identical pattern survives untouched in docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb, which trains with a shuffled fixed-batch `DataLoader` and then computes its 'Theoretical epsilon' with `sample_rate = batch_size / len(train_data)` and `total_steps = n_epochs * (len(train_data) // batch_size)` fed into `dpsgd_acc.poisson(...)`. Shuffled fixed-size batching is not Poisson subsampling, and the floor division under-counts the batches the loader actually yields (`drop_last` defaults to False).
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced with the notebook's own constants (n_samples=500, batch_size=64, n_epochs=200, nm=0.5, delta=1e-5): `cf.train_subset` yields 252 rows at HEAD, so the loader yields 4 batches/epoch = 800 steps, while the notebook computes `200 * (252 // 64) = 600`. Poisson-amplified epsilon at the documented 600 steps is 250.89; at the 800 steps actually run, 314.46; and with no amplification at all (the honest model for a deterministic shuffled partition in which each record participates once per epoch, 200 participations) 519.70. The published number the reader sees is the smallest of the three. The notebook then prints 'OK: audited epsilon is within the theoretical bound', teaching that this is the way to compute the bound an audit is checked against. It is not executed by CI.
evidence: docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb cell 9: `train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)` — fixed-size shuffled batches, no Opaque sampler

Same notebook cell 13: `sample_rate = batch_size / len(train_data)` ; `total_steps = n_epochs * (len(train_data) // batch_size)` ; `process = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), sample_rate) * total_steps`
Measured at HEAD: len(cf.train_subset(dataset)) = 252 (the notebook's stored output says 263), len(train_loader) = 4, documented total_steps = 600, actual = 800
Measured epsilons: 600 steps -> 250.89 ; 800 steps -> 314.46 ; unamplified 200 participations -> 519.70

Contrast docs/tutorials/dp_sgd_training.ipynb cell 13, which was fixed: `sampler = PoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate=sample_rate, n_steps=total_steps, key=key(43))` with the comment 'The sampler and accountant use the same independent-inclusion process.'
.github/workflows/pr.yml:293-302 does not include privacy_auditing.ipynb
findings.fix_sketch: Switch the tutorial's training loop to `PoissonSampler(train_data, sample_rate=..., n_steps=total_steps, key=...)` as dp_sgd_training.ipynb now does, or keep the shuffled loader and price it without Poisson amplification; either way derive `total_steps` from `len(train_loader) * n_epochs` rather than floor division, and add the notebook to the pr.yml execution list.

findings.title: "Documented privacy examples execute in CI" is a partial check: zero of 369 markdown snippets run, 4 of 7 tutorials are never executed, and no executed notebook's published output is ever compared to a fresh run
findings.claim: HEAD (12146ec4, 'docs(accounting): execute documented privacy examples (#1034)') added one CI step. What it actually covers: `examples/quickstart.py`; `python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py`; and `jupyter execute` on copies of 3 of the 7 tutorial notebooks. What it does not cover: (a) the 369 fenced ```python blocks across 46 docs/*.md pages — nothing executes them (`grep -n doctest pyproject.toml conftest.py` finds nothing, there is no doctest-glob, no markdown plugin); (b) distributed_training.ipynb, llm_finetuning.ipynb, privacy_auditing.ipynb and sampling_and_microbatching.ipynb, all four in the mkdocs nav (mkdocs.yml:139-145), three of which carry stored outputs that are published verbatim; (c) the other 7 `examples/*.py`; (d) any numeric assertion in the doctest — running it with `-v` shows '4 tests in 1 items, 4 passed', and all four are bare statements with no expected output, so it is an import smoke test. Finally, the notebooks are copied to `$RUNNER_TEMP` before `--inplace`, while mkdocs.yml:60-61 sets `mkdocs-jupyter: execute: false`, so the docs site serves the committed outputs and CI never compares them to a fresh run. And `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (push to main) has no docs job at all, so this check exists only on PRs.

findings.title: Paired second-moment accounting is documented as unconditionally equal to the first-moment mechanism; the equality only holds when the second-moment strategy's participation blow-up does not exceed the first's, which is neither documented nor enforced
findings.line: 336-338 ('privacy accounting is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism'); same claim at docs/reference/noise.md:85-90; docs/limitations.md:8-9 repeats the benign framing
findings.claim: The Mahalanobis allocation argument the docs give is correct as far as it goes: `paired_noise_stddevs` sets sigma^i_g = nm*sqrt(Delta^i_g * S) with S = sum(Delta^1 + Delta^2), and sum_{g,i} (Delta^i_g/sigma^i_g)^2 = 1/nm^2 exactly (verified numerically to 1e-16 for scalar and PerGroup). But for DP-FTRL the runtime sizes both streams from SINGLE-participation column norms — packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_second_moment.py:140-145 computes `c1` and `c2` with `min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1` — while the accountant prices the first stream at the actual multi-participation sensitivity. Writing rho_i = sens_multi_i / sens_single_i, the joint Mahalanobis sensitivity equals the accounted one iff rho_2 <= rho_1; when rho_2 > rho_1 the realized release exceeds the accounted budget by sqrt((D1*rho_1^2 + D2*rho_2^2)/(rho_1^2*(D1+D2))). Nothing enforces rho_2 <= rho_1: `mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...)` accepts an arbitrary, different-family strategy. This is the delta on open issue #359 ('Define BandMF participation sensitivity and price second moments', blocked/needs-design): the docs assert as settled exactly what that issue tracks as unresolved, and give a BandMF code sample for it.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:71 ('auto-deriving the second-moment strategy is not supported for lambdaCGD. Pass `second_moment_strategy` explicitly') and passes a second-moment strategy whose multi-participation blow-up is larger than the first stream's. Verified accepted with no warning: `mf_gaussian_noise(params, band_mf_strategy(bands=10), second_moment_strategy=bisr_strategy(bandwidth=4), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=10, noise_multiplier=1.0, key=key(0))` constructs successfully. Measured blow-ups at n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=10: band_mf(bands=10) rho=3.1623, bisr(bandwidth=4) rho=3.8106. With D1 ~ D2 that is a ~11% higher realized sensitivity than accounted, i.e. an effective noise multiplier about 10% below the one epsilon was computed from — silently, under a documentation sentence that says accounting 'is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism'.
evidence: docs/reference/accounting.md:336-338: 'The Mahalanobis budget collapses to a single sensitivity-1 Gaussian release at the same noise multiplier, so **privacy accounting is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism**' followed by a `dpftrl_acc.poisson(dpftrl_acc.mf_gaussian(1.0, strategy), ...)` sample

findings.title: BLT parameter table publishes a non-existent `error` knob and a `max_buffers` range whose upper half is hard-rejected — the half of OPQ-358 that the closed sweeps did not fix
findings.claim: OPQ-358 cited two locations: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:129,143 and docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md:190-191. The training-arguments half is fixed (the mf_blt default is now `{"max_buffers": 10}` at training-arguments.md:150, matching _training_arguments.py:259; `noise_calibration_kwargs` defaults now read `{"min": 0.11, "max": 10.0, "tolerance": 1e-3}`, matching _training_arguments.py:1048). The blt.md half is not. The table still lists `error | "max" or "mean" | Error metric to optimize`, but `error` is not a parameter of `blt_strategy` or of anything on the public BLT surface — it is hard-coded to `"max"` at packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_blt.py:83. And it still publishes `max_buffers | 1 - 20 (default 10)` where values above 15 are rejected outright. The table also omits the two parameters `blt_strategy` really takes besides `max_buffers`: `momentum` and `lr_schedule`.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader following the table's advice bullet ('`error = "max"` is the safe choice for worst-case guarantees. `"mean"` optimizes average error ... but gives worse worst-case behavior') looks for a knob that does not exist, and concludes the library is silently choosing one of them. A reader who picks a value from the published `1 - 20` range above 15 gets `ConfigurationError: max_buffers > 15 will likely cause numerical issues` at the first epsilon query — reproduced for 16 and 25.
evidence: docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md:195 `| \`error\` | \`"max"\` or \`"mean"\` | Error metric to optimize. \`"max"\` is conservative. |`
docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/blt.md:196 `| \`max_buffers\` | 1 - 20 (default 10) | ... |`
`inspect.signature(blt_strategy)` -> `(*, max_buffers: 'int' = 10, momentum: 'float' = 1.0, lr_schedule: 'Schedule | None' = None)` — no `error`
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_blt.py:83 `error="max",` hard-coded inside `_blt_optimize_cached`

Executed: `blt_strategy(max_buffers=16)` then `mf_gaussian(1.0, s, n_steps=500, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5)` -> `ConfigurationError: max_buffers > 15 will likely cause numerical issues.` (same for 25)
Fixed sibling: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:150 `mf_blt | balls_in_bins | {"max_buffers": 10}` matches _training_arguments.py:259
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the `error` row and its Tips bullet (or expose the parameter if it is meant to be user-selectable), change the `max_buffers` range to `1 - 15 (default 10)` to match the validator, and add the `momentum` and `lr_schedule` rows that the signature actually has.

findings.title: The README and installation guide's extras block installs an unrelated PyPI project named `opaque`; six of the ten distribution names are unclaimed on PyPI
findings.claim: The documented primary install correctly pins the JetBrains index (`pip install opaque --index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` — verified reachable anonymously, HTTP 200, serving opaque 0.15.x wheels and all ten sub-distributions). But the 'Extras' block immediately below it drops the index: `pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`. Those resolve against PyPI, where the name `opaque` belongs to a different project (version 1.0.0, author Stefan Marsiske, homepage https://github.com/stef/libopaque, summary 'python libopaque wrapper'). pip only warns about an unknown extra, so the copy-pasted command installs that package. AGENTS.md's installation matrix (lines 127-137) is index-less too: `pip install opaque-base`, `opaque-engine`, `opaque-dpsgd`, `opaque-patches`, `opaque-transformers` are all unregistered on PyPI (HTTP 404), so those names are open to takeover. Defensive dependency-confusion stubs at version 999.9.9 were published on 2026-08-12 for only four of the ten names (opaque-accounting, opaque-auditing, opaque-dpftrl, opaque-optimizers). Marble #559 ('migrate package publishing to a JetBrains-managed registry') and #574 ('remediate dependency security alerts before public visibility') are both closed; neither covered this.
findings.failure_scenario: A user reads the install page top to bottom, runs `pip install "opaque[all]"` from the extras block, gets a WARNING about an unprovided extra, and ends up with `libopaque` installed under the `opaque` import name — every `import opaque.dpsgd...` then fails, or (worse, if they already installed the real wheels) the foreign distribution replaces the namespace root. For the six unregistered sub-names, anyone can claim `opaque-dpsgd` on PyPI and be installed by anybody following AGENTS.md's matrix or by any resolver that falls back to PyPI.
evidence: README.md:77-81 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:31-36 — four `pip install "opaque[...]"` commands with no `--index-url`, directly under a block that does pin it
`curl https://pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json` -> name opaque, version 1.0.0, author 'Stefan Marsiske', home_page 'https://github.com/stef/libopaque', summary 'python libopaque wrapper'

PyPI presence of the ten distribution names: opaque-base 404, opaque-engine 404, opaque-dpsgd 404, opaque-patches 404, opaque-transformers 404, opaque-alignment 404; opaque-dpftrl/opaque-accounting/opaque-auditing/opaque-optimizers all 200 at version 999.9.9 with description 'This public copy of the package is a stub published on pypi.org designed to mitigate risks from Dependency Confusion.' uploaded 2026-08-12
JetBrains index carries all ten (HTTP 200 for each `.../simple/<name>/`), so the pinned command is sound
AGENTS.md:127-137 'Installation matrix' — index-less `pip install opaque-base` ... `pip install "opaque[all]"`
findings.fix_sketch: Repeat `--index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` on every command in the extras blocks of README.md and docs/getting-started/installation.md (or show a `pip.conf` / `[tool.uv.index]` snippet once and reference it), do the same in AGENTS.md's matrix, and register the remaining six defensive stubs on PyPI alongside the four already published.

findings.title: The RNG-key guide's reproducibility snippet raises InputTypeError — the sibling page of the OPQ-362 fix
findings.claim: OPQ-362 ('`docs/reference/rng.md` calls `gaussian_noise` positionally and binds its 2-tuple to a single name') was closed in sweep #843, and HEAD does rewrite docs/reference/rng.md. The 'Reproducibility' snippet in the companion user-guide page still passes a bare dict to the noise function, which HEAD rejects. Executed verbatim it fails at line 8 with `opaque.api.base.exceptions.InputTypeError: gaussian_noise expects ClippedPytree inputs. Wrap manual values with opaque.types.clipped(...).` The page's stated point (identical keys reproduce identical noise) is never demonstrated.
evidence: docs/user-guide/rng-key.md:279 `grads = {"w": torch.randn(100)}` then :282 `noisy1, _ = noise_fn(grads, s1)`

Every epsilon and noise-multiplier value stored in docs/tutorials/accounting_and_calibration.ipynb was recomputed against HEAD and matches to the published precision: 0.7181 / 6.67e-07 (cell 3), 1.2656 / 3.0000 (cell 7), 1.8283 / 2.61e-03 / 0.1612 (cell 11), 0.1898 / 2.3995 / 2.4074 (cell 13), 0.4062 (cell 15). The multi-target calibration table in cell 9 was spot-checked at eps=3.0.

docs/tutorials/dp_ftrl_training.ipynb's published numbers were recomputed: single-participation sensitivity 1.0000, calibrated noise multiplier 4.1981, achieved epsilon 3.00 — all match. Its sample-rate derivation (`sample_rate = batch_size * bands / n_samples`, cell 5) is the correct conditional-rate form, in contrast to the reference pages flagged above.

docs/tutorials/dp_sgd_training.ipynb is the fixed version of OPQ-355: cell 13 drives the loop from `PoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate=..., n_steps=total_steps, key=...)` and composes `dpsgd_acc.poisson(...) * step` at the actual step count. I read every cell and found no residual shuffled/fixed-batch pricing.

The k-out-of-t 'block bound dominates total allocation' claim (docs/reference/sampling.md:120-124, docs/user-guide/sampling.md:245-247) is mathematically sound, and I derived it independently rather than taking the comment's word: with iid per-step observations, the add/remove likelihood ratio is E_S[prod_{i in S} Z_i] with Z_i iid and E[Z_i]=1; symmetrizing any distribution on k-subsets over a uniform permutation of [t] gives the uniform distribution on k-subsets (S_t acts transitively), so the total-allocation ratio is the pi-average of block-allocation ratios; the hockey-stick functional (x - e^eps)_+ is convex and the reference measure is exchangeable, so Jensen gives H_eps(total) <= H_eps(block). The argument survives unequal blocks, and packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:186-194 splits t into m_f blocks of floor(t/k) and m_c of ceil(t/k) rather than assuming divisibility.

The paired second-moment Mahalanobis identity published at docs/reference/noise.md:56-90 is exact, verified both algebraically (sum_{g,i} (Delta/sigma)^2 = sum Delta/(nm^2 S) = 1/nm^2) and numerically through `paired_noise_stddevs` for scalar and PerGroup bounds (0.5917159763313611 vs 1/1.3^2 = 0.5917159763313609). The worst case is attainable (a 1-sparse clipped gradient makes ||g^2||_2 = ||g||^2), so the reduction to a sensitivity-1 Gaussian is tight, not merely an upper bound — for the single-participation case. The multi-participation DP-FTRL caveat is reported as a finding above.

The RNG domain-separation table at docs/reference/rng.md:218-232 is accurate: all twelve published tags were matched against the string constants in the source (GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, ADAPTIVE_CLIPPING_STREAM_FOLD, POISSON_STREAM_FOLD, K_OUT_OF_T_STREAM_FOLD, MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, SECOND_MOMENT_FIRST/SECOND_STREAM_FOLD, CYCLIC_POISSON_STREAM_FOLD, B_MIN_SEP_STREAM_FOLD, BALLS_IN_BINS_STREAM_FOLD, PAIRED_FIRST/SECOND_STREAM_FOLD, _CANARY_SELECTION_DOMAIN, _COIN_FLIP_DOMAIN, IGNORE_DATA_SKIP_STREAM_FOLD), each present verbatim.

docs/user-guide/precision.md was rewritten by 7f55aae5 and every checkable claim holds: `clipped_grad` defaults to `compute_dtype=None`; `gaussian_noise` and `mf_gaussian_noise` both default to `compute_dtype=torch.float32` (verified via inspect.signature). The `opaque.precision` facade is genuinely gone from the tree (only an untracked empty directory remains locally), and no doc, README, AGENTS.md or mkdocs nav entry still advertises it.

The three breaking removals leave no stale user-facing references to the removed capability: `grep -rni 'bounded_gaussian|bounded gaussian|bounded noise'` over docs/, README.md, all package READMEs, examples/, AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md returns nothing; `grep -rni 'per_step|PerStep|random_allocation|loss_scal|GradScaler|dynamic loss'` returns only unrelated hits (the surviving `Accountant(prefix=)` / `calibrate(prefix=)` feature, whose signatures I confirmed still exist, and prose uses of 'prefix' in alignment/BISR/BLT). training-arguments.md's horizon story ('every privacy metric reported during the run is the conservative full-horizon epsilon') matches the post-#894 behavior.

OPQ-356/357/358/359/364/365/367/368/369 spot-checks all passed at HEAD: `dpsgd_acc.adaclip` now exposes `num_groups` and it is documented at docs/reference/accounting.md:321-323; the `opaque.accounting` module docstring names only factories that exist (verified by importing each of gaussian/adaclip/poisson/parallel_poisson/k_out_of_t and mf_gaussian/poisson/b_min_sep/balls_in_bins); mf_blt default `{"max_buffers": 10}` and `noise_calibration_kwargs` `{"min": 0.11, "max": 10.0, "tolerance": 1e-3}` match _training_arguments.py:259 and :1048; `privacy_target_delta` is documented and implemented as `1/dataset_size**1.1` (_training_arguments.py:265-270); SquareChiPO is gone from docs and `chunked_nll` is documented; docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:143-164 now terminates, composes the accountant, and calls `optimizer.update(noised, opt_state, params=params)`.

A static kwarg/positional checker run over all 370 extracted docs snippets against the real signatures found exactly one drift (the bsr.md case reported above); no snippet imports a name that does not exist, and no `alias.attr` reference in any snippet fails to resolve. A separate scan of all 14 distinct backticked `opaque.*` dotted names in docs prose found only the one bad path (docs/reference/distributed.md:82) plus the RNG tag strings, which are not API names.

Executing all 370 extracted snippets in isolation produced 296 failures, of which every one except the four reported was either a NameError on a deliberate placeholder, a signature-fragment SyntaxError in a reference API block, or an environment precondition (torch.distributed not initialized, a checkpoint file absent, bf16 unavailable). I triaged the full list rather than sampling.

The lr_schedule deprecation claims in docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:47 and lambda-cgd.md:50 ('Deprecated compatibility argument; only `None` is accepted') are accurate: passing a real schedule to either factory raises ConfigurationError ('BisrStrategy/LambdaCgdStrategy does not support lr_schedule').

The auditing canary-ceiling table at docs/user-guide/auditing.md:226-230 is internally consistent with its own formula eps <~ ln(m / -ln(alpha)) at alpha=0.05: 5.81, 8.11, 10.42, 12.72 for m = 1e3..1e6, matching the published 5.8 / 8.1 / 10.4 / 12.7. `estimate.attack_auc(confidence=, num_samples=, key=)` matches the documented signature and the documented requirement that `key` is mandatory when `confidence` is given.

docs/mechanisms/dp-sgd/gaussian.md's mathematics is correct: the privacy loss l(x) = (Delta/sigma^2)(Delta/2 - x) is the correct log-ratio of the two normal densities, and the hockey-stick expression delta(eps) = Phi(Delta/2sigma - eps*sigma/Delta) - e^eps*Phi(-Delta/2sigma - eps*sigma/Delta) is the standard analytic Gaussian mechanism formula. The one soft spot is the pedagogical line 'a sample rate of 1% makes the mechanism behave as if noise were 100x larger' — true in the RDP/moments sense but not at the (eps, delta) level, where a single step of poisson(gaussian(1.0), 0.01) gives eps=0.1995 against gaussian(100)'s eps=0.0272 at delta=1e-5 (7.3x apart; 1.83 vs 1.20 after 1000 compositions). It is hedged with 'roughly' and drives no published value, so I did not file it.

examples/quickstart.py, the file the Quick Start page now includes (`--8<-- "examples/quickstart.py:4:"` with pymdownx.snippets enabled at mkdocs.yml:70), runs green end to end in this environment, reaches exactly epsilon=3.00 at step 310, and carries two real assertions (`assert step == num_steps` and `abs(final_epsilon - result.achieved) < 1e-9`) that tie the reported epsilon to the calibration. Its sampler (PoissonSampler at q = 32/1000) and accountant (`poisson(gaussian(nm), q) * num_steps`) are the same process.

The documented JetBrains package index is genuinely public and complete: `https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` returns 200 anonymously and carries all ten distribution names plus `opaque` 0.15.x wheels, so the pinned `--index-url` form of the install instructions works as written (the index-less extras block is the defect, reported above).

docs/user-guide/sampling.md's b-min-sep section does document the sampler/accountant conversion the reference page omits: lines 190-213 give `p = p_0 / (1 - p_0 * (bands - 1))` and it matches `participation_p_from_per_example_rate` in packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/__init__.py:38-59 exactly, including the bands==1 special case.

The trainer's sampler allow-lists match their documentation: `_ALLOWED_SAMPLERS`, `_SAMPLING_KWARGS`, `_CLIPPING_KWARGS` and `_SAMPLER_BY_MECHANISM` in _training_arguments.py:195-240 agree row for row with the tables in docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:134-165, including the claim that modes other than poisson and k_out_of_t accept no sampling kwargs, and the rejection of plain `poisson` for mf_band. (`_MECHANISM_KWARGS['gaussian']` still contains the dead `"bound"` key, but __post_init__ raises on it first, so it is unreachable rather than a documentation defect.)

A 200-trial null-calibration study of the one-run auditor (random scores independent of membership, m=1000, both the mu-GDP and eps-delta methods) was started but did not finish within the session budget, so I am making no claim about the calibration of `OneRunEstimate.epsilon_at` under the null. That question is tracked by open issues #376 and #828 and I deliberately did not file a duplicate; the observation I would flag if it were confirmed is that neither docs/user-guide/auditing.md nor docs/limitations.md carries any caveat about it, while auditing.md:1-6 presents the result as an 'empirical lower bound' whose excess over the theoretical epsilon indicates 'a bug in the implementation'.
